subject: Re: Kickoff: GWikiMatch as the standard long-document matching eval
body:
Anders,

Staffing: Quentin 50%, Bilal 60%, Oyin 50%. Compute is minor - scoring two baselines on long-document pairs needs maybe 16 A100s best-effort for a week each.

The real engineering item surfaced in Bilal's audit of the raw pairs: Wikipedia mirrors, redirects and near-identical revisions create pairs that are effectively the same document twice. If those leak into the benchmark, similarity scores inflate and the eval loses credibility. So: we are scoping and staffing a dataset de-duplication pipeline, built from scratch - Bilal owns the design (shingling + MinHash over document text, plus URL-normalization rules), Oyin the batch infrastructure, working version by 6/19. I am carrying it as a first-class deliverable, since every dataset this portfolio hosts after GWikiMatch will need the same pass.

That pushes the hosted-dataset milestone from 5/29 to 6/26. Baselines and the 8/5 adoption review still hold.

Bao
